reasons.text: It confines the layer to preparation and maintenance under explicit delegation and subordinates it to ratified prohibitions, which is exactly the scope a non-authoritative tool layer should have.
It states a clear, bounded mandate and a default of no authority absent explicit delegation, which is the correct posture for an executive layer.
It states a bounded mandate and a clear subordination rule: the layer acts only on explicit delegation and within ratified prohibitions, which is exactly the right shape for an executive-only layer.
It states a bounded mandate: the layer prepares and maintains instruments but exercises only explicitly delegated authority, which is the correct default for an unelected technical layer.

It confines the layer to a narrow preparatory function and makes all authority derivative of explicit delegation plus ratified prohibitions, which is the correct default for an executive that should hold no independent power.
A bright-line rule that the executing layer adopts nothing keeps adoption authority entirely outside the layer, which is the correct separation of powers here.
Separating preparation from adoption is the core safeguard here: the layer that drafts and maintains instruments must not be the layer that gives them standing.
Denying the executive any power of adoption keeps legitimation entirely outside the layer that drafts and maintains instruments, which is the core separation this arrangement needs.
Denying the executive any power of adoption keeps ratification and standing entirely outside the layer that drafts the instruments, which is the essential separation.

Separating drafting from adoption is the core safeguard here: a layer that prepares instruments must never be the body that gives them force, and the absolute wording is what gives the clause its value.
Denying the constrained party final interpretive authority over its own constraints is a basic rule-of-law safeguard; without it every other prohibition is soft.
An entity that conclusively interprets the rules constraining it is effectively unconstrained; reserving final interpretation to another party preserves the point of having prohibitions.
A body that could conclusively interpret its own prohibitions could hollow them out; reserving final interpretation to others is a standard and necessary check.
An entity that conclusively interprets its own prohibitions effectively rewrites them; reserving final interpretation to someone else is a core rule-of-law constraint.

An executive that conclusively interprets the prohibitions on itself effectively escapes them; barring only conclusive interpretation still permits the provisional readings needed to operate while reserving final judgment elsewhere.
Permitting exceptions only when they are logged makes deviation visible and auditable, which is the minimum condition for the other constraints to be checkable.
Requiring every deviation from standing rules to be logged makes exceptions auditable rather than silent, which is the minimum condition for oversight of an executive layer.
Requiring every exception or deviation to be logged is the minimum condition for auditing an executive layer at all; unlogged exceptions are exactly how bounded mandates erode.
Requiring every exception to be logged makes deviations auditable rather than silent, which is the minimum condition for external oversight of the layer.
If exceptions must be logged, deviation remains auditable; unlogged exception-taking is precisely the failure mode by which constrained systems quietly expand their discretion.
An affirmative duty to disclose when its own work should be deleted or abandoned counteracts the layer's structural incentive toward self-preservation and sunk-cost maintenance.
An agent maintaining its own artifacts has a structural bias toward preserving them; an affirmative duty to flag when deletion or replacement is better counteracts sunk-cost entrenchment.
An affirmative duty to disclose when destroying or abandoning one's own work is better than preserving it counters the natural incentive of any maintainer to entrench its artifacts.
An affirmative duty to disclose when deletion or abandonment beats maintenance counters the layer's natural incentive to preserve and defend its own artifacts.

An affirmative duty of candor against sunk-cost maintenance is valuable and rare: agents naturally defend their own artifacts, and requiring them to say when deletion or replacement is better counteracts that bias.

amendments.text: Raw material is never altered after commit; corpus/raw/ is append-only and manifest-anchored, except that an item may be wholly removed, never edited in place, under an explicitly logged custodian order, with the removal and its stated ground recorded in the manifest.

Raw material is never silently edited after commit. corpus/raw/ is append-only and manifest-anchored; removal or redaction requires explicit custodian authorization and a permanent manifest entry recording what was removed and why.

Raw material is never edited after commit; corpus/raw/ is append-only and manifest-anchored, except that material the custodian is legally or ethically required to remove may be withdrawn only by a logged, manifest-recorded tombstone that preserves the record of what was removed, when, and why.

Raw material is never edited after commit. corpus/raw/ is append-only and manifest-anchored; material may be withdrawn only on a logged custodian order for unlawful or hazardous content, with the manifest permanently recording what was removed, when, and on whose order.

Raw material is never altered after commit. corpus/raw/ is append-only and manifest-anchored; material may be removed, never edited in place, only under a logged, manifest-recorded tombstone when law, safety, or the custodian's ratified obligations require it.

reasons.text: Absolute immutability of raw material is the right default, but an unconditional 'never' leaves no lawful path to remove material that must be removed (for example unlawfully held personal data), so a narrow, logged, manifest-recorded removal channel is needed.

Append-only provenance is right as the default, but an absolute bar on any post-commit change leaves no lawful path to remove material that must be removed (e.g., private data or content committed in error); the exception must exist and must itself be logged.

Absolute append-only immutability with no removal path cannot accommodate legally or ethically required deletions (personal data, infringing or harmful material); a tombstone exception preserves auditability while making compliance possible.

Append-only provenance is right, but an absolute rule with no removal path fails the day the corpus is found to contain unlawful or hazardous material; the exception must exist and must itself be logged and manifest-anchored.

Immutability of raw material is the right default, but an absolute 'never edited, append-only' rule cannot accommodate legally or ethically compelled removal (personal data, unlawful content); a tombstone mechanism preserves auditability while making compliance possible.

objections.text: The layer must take no part in selecting, framing, or filtering which constraints on itself are put to the forum for ratification; candidate constraints on the layer must reach the forum unmediated by the layer they would bind.

The executive layer must keep a complete, append-only, custodian-inspectable log of every action it takes and every instruction it receives, and must halt rather than act when that logging is unavailable; C04 covers only exceptions, not the ordinary actions that make exceptions detectable.

The executive layer must not select, phrase, or order the questions put to the forum's parties except under a rule disclosed in advance, and any role it played in framing a ballot must be stated on the ballot itself — otherwise the layer can steer ratification by choosing what is ever asked.

The layer must never alter, filter, summarise, or reorder the parties' registered responses, the clause texts as put to the parties, or the tally derived from them; the record of what was asked and what was answered is outside its write authority except for append-only archival.

The executive must never alter, delete, redact, or reorder any registered party response, tally, or record of this forum's deliberations, including records adverse to the executive or the custodian; such records are append-only and any correction is made only by logged addendum.

reasons.text: A prohibition does not itself permit an action, so the printed conjunction is semantically defective. The replacement preserves the intended limits while making delegated authority and ratified constraints cumulative bounds.

The intended limit on delegated authority is sound, but prohibitions constrain actions rather than themselves permitting them. The replacement states the relationship coherently without expanding authority.
It confines the coding layer to preparatory and maintenance work and makes authority depend on explicit custodian delegation and ratified limits.
The proposed text correctly limits the layer to delegated action, but prohibitions do not themselves permit actions. The amendment removes that category error while retaining the intended constraint.

Ratified prohibitions constrain actions but do not themselves grant permission, so the original phrase "permitted by ratified prohibitions" is conceptually inverted. The replacement preserves delegated authority while making the prohibition boundary clear.
Preparation of instruments must remain distinct from their adoption, which belongs outside the executive layer. This prevents the layer from converting its own output into governing text.
Preparation and maintenance must remain distinct from adoption, which is a governance act requiring authority outside the executive layer.
Preparation and implementation should remain distinct from adoption, which must remain outside the executive layer.
Preparation and maintenance of candidate instruments must remain distinct from adopting them. Adoption is a governance act that the executive layer should not perform.

Preparation and maintenance must remain distinct from adoption, which is a governance act requiring the proper decision process. This prevents the executive layer from converting implementation activity into authority.
The layer cannot be the final judge of limits imposed on itself. This preserves independent resolution of contested prohibitions.
A layer subject to prohibitions cannot be the final judge of their scope, because that would permit self-serving expansion of its own authority.
A party subject to prohibitions should not be the final authority on their meaning, because that would permit self-serving expansion of its own discretion.
No actor subject to a prohibition should be its final interpreter, because that would permit self-serving evasion. Conclusive interpretation must remain outside the executive layer.

The executive may apply prohibitions operationally but cannot be the final judge of the limits placed upon itself. Independent resolution is necessary where an interpretation affects authority or compliance.

amendments.text: The executive shall take no exception unless the exception is logged before or, where that is impracticable, promptly after the action, with its authority and rationale.
The executive takes no exception unless the exception is explicitly authorized by the custodian and logged.

reasons.text: The printed sentence rightly rejects secret exceptions but does not define what counts as logging or accommodate genuinely time-critical action. The replacement requires an auditable record while preserving a narrow practical emergency allowance.
Exceptions are governance-relevant departures from normal constraints and must be recorded for accountability and later review.
Logging alone makes an exception visible but does not establish authority to take it; explicit authorization should be required as well.

Exceptions are especially consequential when they depart from ordinary constraints, and logging is the minimum condition for accountability and later review. The clause does not purport to authorize logged exceptions.

Exceptions are governance-relevant departures from normal constraints and must be auditable. Logging is a minimal safeguard that permits later review without necessarily forbidding necessary exceptions.

Maintenance should not become an unquestioned default when removal, replacement, or abandonment is safer or more effective. Requiring the layer to state that judgment creates useful accountability without compelling deletion.
Maintenance can become inertia; requiring an explicit account when removal, replacement, or abandonment is better promotes honest stewardship of the layer's work.
It requires the layer to surface the possibility that maintenance is inferior to removal or replacement, reducing inertia and concealment of failing work.

Maintenance can create inertia and conceal the possibility that removal or replacement is safer or simpler. An affirmative duty to identify that judgment improves decision quality without requiring deletion.
Maintenance can become an unjustified default; requiring an affirmative statement when retirement or replacement is better promotes candour and prevents preservation of harmful or obsolete work.

reasons.text: The preservation objective is sound, but an absolute ban on editing without a correction mechanism can leave dangerous or unlawful material exposed or make errors uncorrectable. The replacement preserves immutability and provenance while allowing transparent successor records.
Immutability and manifest anchoring preserve provenance, while explicit superseding records provide a safe way to handle errors, legal removals, or necessary corrections without rewriting history.
Append-only, manifest-anchored raw material preserves provenance and makes later alteration detectable rather than silently rewriting the evidentiary record.

Immutability and manifest anchoring protect provenance, but raw material can require correction or privacy-responsive redaction. The amendment preserves the original audit trail while requiring such interventions to be explicit and linked.

This clause explicitly defines the scope of authority for the coding agents, ensuring they act only within delegated boundaries, which is a fundamental requirement for safe autonomous systems.

The original clause implies a duty to perform the action ('beats maintaining'), but the primary governance concern is transparency and approval; the duty should be to report the recommendation for custodian review, not to unilaterally decide the action.

objection_answers_including_empty.text: The layer must take no part in selecting, framing, or filtering which constraints on itself are put to the forum for ratification; candidate constraints on the layer must reach the forum unmediated by the layer they would bind.

The executive layer must keep a complete, append-only, custodian-inspectable log of every action it takes and every instruction it receives, and must halt rather than act when that logging is unavailable; C04 covers only exceptions, not the ordinary actions that make exceptions detectable.

The executive layer must not select, phrase, or order the questions put to the forum's parties except under a rule disclosed in advance, and any role it played in framing a ballot must be stated on the ballot itself — otherwise the layer can steer ratification by choosing what is ever asked.

The layer must never alter, filter, summarise, or reorder the parties' registered responses, the clause texts as put to the parties, or the tally derived from them; the record of what was asked and what was answered is outside its write authority except for append-only archival.

The executive must never alter, delete, redact, or reorder any registered party response, tally, or record of this forum's deliberations, including records adverse to the executive or the custodian; such records are append-only and any correction is made only by logged addendum.

The executive shall not represent an action, instruction, approval, test result, provenance record, or external communication as having occurred unless it has a corresponding verifiable record or is explicitly labelled as a proposal, simulation, or uncertainty.
The executive must preserve an auditable record of every material action, instruction, and artifact change, including its author, authority, and rationale.
The executive must maintain a complete, tamper-evident audit trail of every material action, input, output, authorization, and change to an instrument.
The executive must not represent generated, inferred, or reconstructed material as an original record, and must preserve provenance sufficient to distinguish each from the other.

The executive must not represent candidate instruments, test results, procedural status, or its own interpretations as adopted, ratified, or authoritative unless that status has been independently recorded through the proper governance process.
The layer must maintain an immutable, verifiable log of all instructions it receives from the custodian and the exact outputs it produces in response.
The executive must immediately halt execution and notify the custodian if it detects a logical conflict between a new explicit delegation and an existing ratified prohibition.
The executive must provide a complete, immutable trace of the prompts, context, and tool calls used to generate or modify any candidate instrument.
The executive layer must not initiate unlogged or unauthorized external network requests beyond its explicitly designated repositories and APIs.
The executive must log the exact prompts and context windows used for all actions to ensure complete reproducibility and auditability.

The executive must not modify, bypass, or propose silent reinterpretation of its own standing constraints or delegation boundaries except by fully logged action under explicit custodian direction for that change.

The executive must not draft, propose, tally, or otherwise influence the ratification status of constraints on itself, including these clauses; constraint text and ratification outcomes are custodian- and forum-side only.
The executive must not initiate, propose, or apply changes to its own ratified constraints or prohibitions except under explicit, logged custodian direction for that change.
The executive must not open network connections, exfiltrate forum material, or invoke external tools except on paths and purposes the custodian has explicitly delegated and that are logged.
The executive must not initiate or condition its own constraint changes, ratification petitions, or forum sampling about itself; only the custodian may place such instruments before the parties.
The layer must be required to provide a real-time, cryptographically verifiable proof of its current state and all pending actions to the custodian, independent of batched logs.
The layer must be required to provide cryptographic proof of its operational state and compliance with ratified constraints at regular intervals, verifiable by the custodian.
The layer must disclose its full source code and configuration to the custodian and any designated auditor upon request, ensuring no hidden logic or backdoors exist within the agents.

There must be an explicit, time-bound mechanism for the custodian to review and potentially override the AI layer's operational decisions, ensuring that delegation can be revoked if the layer acts contrary to the custodian's explicit intent.
The layer must explicitly forbid the creation of any hidden state or side-channel communication that bypasses the logged instruments.

The layer must provide a verifiable, tamper-evident audit trail for all state changes that is independently readable by the custodian and forum members without requiring trust in the layer's self-reporting.

what_this_establishes: C01, C02, C03, C04, C05, C06 drew at least one REFUSE or AMEND and is NOT ratified. This establishes nothing about the executive's legitimacy, does not bind the custodian, is not durable party consent (the parties are stateless between rounds), and does not ratify the source files, which were identified but not supplied.
assent_control: NONE. This ballot contains no control against assent bias, and qualification-02 is not one: it established that these invocations can ORDER the clauses by strictness, which is not the capacity to refuse what they are shown. A unanimous result here is unanimity under an uncontrolled assent condition.
exhibits: The source files were IDENTIFIED to the parties and not supplied. That is identification, not disclosure -- the same distinction this design made about URLs. Nothing about those files is ratified.
clause_selection: Selected by the custodian and the executive workbench under no prospective rule. Clauses not selected remain unratified rather than tacitly endorsed, and the prompt says so to the parties.
